chunks.title: [Cantonese Subtitled Dubbing] CLO Official Tutorial Video ~ Basics Part p02 2. Creating a Multi-Piece Patchwork Jacket
chunks.content: ## Introduction to Loading and Preparing the Jacket Model in CLO This section explains how to load a men's jacket model and related pattern files into CLO, including working with the avatar, pattern files, and adjustment sheet tools to prepare the workspace for patchwork jacket creation. - Open the picture window and double-click the file named **avatar**. - Navigate to **mirv2** and open the file **mv2henry.mvt** by double-clicking or dragging it into the 3D window. - Open the **printfiles** folder in the picture window. - Locate the **B-Basic B-Jumper** folder (installed via cloud for the tutorial). - Double-click or drag **jumper-mirv.dxf** into the 2D or 3D window. - Use the **Adjustment Sheet Tool** in the 2D window to arrange the sheets together for easier later manipulation. ## Pattern Piece Editing and Sheet Arrangement This section details editing pattern pieces, removing unnecessary parts, and setting symmetrical and linked versions through the 2D tool channels, focusing on preparing the pattern pieces accurately. - In the 2D tool channel, use **编辑版片工具 (Edit Pattern Piece Tool)** and right-click on the middle bar. - Exit the menu and select **Simple Chain** mode. - Use the **Adjustment Sheets Tool** to select sheets and remove the middle section and steam from the frame. - Choose options for **column-linked version** and **symmetrical version** to maintain consistency in editing. ## Using 3D Window Tools for Model Visualization and Panel Assignment This section covers using the 3D vertical toolbar to display key points on the model and assign pattern panels correctly in the 3D space to ensure proper alignment. - In the 3D window, select the **3D vertical toolbar #4**. - Click the **Display Point** icon (second icon in the level display virtual model series) to show blue points around the 3D model. - In the 2D window, press **Ctrl + A** to select all panels, then move them up to remove blocked points. - Assign panels by left-clicking around the model in the 3D window, switching views as needed (front and rear views). - Position the **collar plate** on the center point of the back neck. - Position the **sleeve plate** above the arm. - Use the fourth icon of the 3D vertical toolbar to toggle display of arrangement points on or off. ## Sewing Pattern Pieces Using the Line Sewing Tool This section explains the detailed sewing process of the jacket pieces, emphasizing the importance of sewing direction and order for assembling front, back, sleeves, collar, and bottom parts. - Select the **Line Sewing Tool** in the 2D window. - Sew front and back panels together, ensuring correct sewing direction. - Sew sleeves to the armhole, maintaining correct direction. - Sew the collar to the neckline, selecting the collar plate and collar line while holding the **Shift** key to maintain proper alignment. - Sew the bottom edge of the jacket, checking seam line correctness by rotating the 3D window.

chunks.title: [Cantonese Subtitled Dubbing] CLO Official Tutorial Video ~ Basics Part p02 2. Creating a Multi-Piece Patchwork Jacket
chunks.content: ## Sewing Pattern Pieces Using the Line Sewing Tool This section explains the detailed sewing process of the jacket pieces, emphasizing the importance of sewing direction and order for assembling front, back, sleeves, collar, and bottom parts. - Select the **Line Sewing Tool** in the 2D window. - Sew front and back panels together, ensuring correct sewing direction. - Sew sleeves to the armhole, maintaining correct direction. - Sew the collar to the neckline, selecting the collar plate and collar line while holding the **Shift** key to maintain proper alignment. - Sew the bottom edge of the jacket, checking seam line correctness by rotating the 3D window. ## Using 3D Toolbar and Zipper Attachment This section describes using the 3D toolbar to simulate clothing assembly and automatically attach zippers based on seam line relationships. - Open the 3D toolbar and select the **3D Clothing** tool. - Click and drag from the top of the collar plate to the bottom of the clothing plate, repeating for both sides. - The **3D zipper** function automatically finds the add-on object according to seam line relationships for correct zipper placement. - Press the **Simulation** button to bind the pattern naturally to the model. - Close the simulation once the binding is complete. ## Applying Materials and Adjusting Model Position This section guides changing the model's pose, applying fabric materials, and managing the simulation process for realistic visualization. - Open the taskbar and enter the **mealv2** file address. - Open the **PoS** file address and load **mv203** file into the 3D window. - Change the model’s position to vertical. - In the drawing window, open the **FABRIK** file. - Drag material into the object window named **FABRIK1**. - Open the simulation to apply the material to the 3D clothing. - Close simulation after completion. ## Manipulating Pull Chains and Hardware Components This section explains how to move and adjust the pull chain and hardware on the zipper using the move tool, including opening, rewinding, and trimming the chain for proper fit. - Select the **Move Tool** in the 3D window. - Click and drag the pull chain along its center line, observing gray shadows for alignment. - Open simulation to animate the upper part of the pull chain opening. - Move and rewind the pull chain along the ruler as needed. - Use the **Trim Hardware** tool to adjust hardware components. - Apply settings to the 3D clothing and close simulation when finished. ## Copying and Adjusting Polyester Tufts and Colors This section covers copying polyester tuft objects, applying color changes in both 2D and 3D views, and using property editors for detailed color adjustments. - Select the polyester tuft in the object window and click **Copy** to duplicate it. - Use **Shift** to select multiple objects. - Apply **Copy On** to the panels from the object window. - Change colors in the property editor, using **Shift** to edit multiple objects simultaneously. - Adjust colors in both 2D and 3D windows for consistent appearance.

chunks.title: [Cantonese Subtitled Dubbing] CLO Official Tutorial Video ~ Basics Part p02 2. Creating a Multi-Piece Patchwork Jacket
chunks.content: ## Copying and Adjusting Polyester Tufts and Colors This section covers copying polyester tuft objects, applying color changes in both 2D and 3D views, and using property editors for detailed color adjustments. - Select the polyester tuft in the object window and click **Copy** to duplicate it. - Use **Shift** to select multiple objects. - Apply **Copy On** to the panels from the object window. - Change colors in the property editor, using **Shift** to edit multiple objects simultaneously. - Adjust colors in both 2D and 3D windows for consistent appearance. ## Customizing Puller Appearance and Material Properties This section details modifying the zipper puller's appearance, including shape and reflection properties, to enhance realism. - In the 3D window, select the pull chain. - Change the puller color and appearance in the attribute editor. - Select **Plastic** as the reflection type to give the puller a plastic-like finish. - Modify the puller's shape and appearance attributes as needed. ## Improving Clothing Quality and Final Color Adjustments This section explains how to use CLO tools to enhance clothing quality and finalize color choices after simulation. - Select the tool to improve clothing quality from the 3D window toolbar and confirm via the menu. - Run the simulation to apply quality improvements to the 3D clothing. - After simulation completes, turn off the simulation. - Select **Nature** for natural fabric appearance. - Use the **Master** button to display and adjust clothing colors. - Add, change, or fine-tune clothing colors as desired. --- This structured guide covers the detailed steps involved in creating a multi-piece patchwork jacket in CLO, from loading files and editing patterns to sewing, simulation, and final appearance adjustments, incorporating important tools and technical terminology essential for fashion design and 3D garment simulation workflows.
